principles.name: Evidence-gated claims
principles.rule: No performance claim ships without a reproducible public benchmark artefact in-repo (make bench regenerates it).

principles.name: Zero-network default
principles.rule: The default install makes zero network calls and requires no API key. Telemetry is opt-in only, consent-prompted at first CLI run.

principles.name: CPU-first
principles.rule: The default install and all default-path SLOs run on CPU-only hardware. No CUDA dependency anywhere in the default dependency tree.

principles.name: Test-first
principles.rule: Write the failing test (TC-XX) before the implementation (FR/AR). Integration tests against local backends preferred over mocks.

principles.name: Typed public API
principles.rule: All public API surfaces fully type-annotated; simulations physically separated from empirical benchmarks under simulations/.

code_style: Optional dependencies isolated behind pip extras

solutions.name: KSE Memory SDK v3 — Universal Hybrid Knowledge Substrate
solutions.client: Open-source (maintainer: Dale Parr; EY-sanctioned personal OSS project)
solutions.scope: Remediate v2.0.0 into a credible, CPU-first, universal hybrid retrieval substrate: honest claims, RRF fusion, user-defined conceptual dimensions, real benchmarks, tiered graph backends.

s1_user_goal.trigger_sentence: When a developer building search over attribute-rich data finds that pure vector retrieval can't answer graded, multi-attribute queries, they need a pip-installable hybrid substrate that fuses embeddings, graph and governed conceptual dimensions locally — fast, with explainable results they can trust.

success.time: Quickstart-to-first-hybrid-result < 60s in a fresh venv, CPU-only, no external services or API key; incremental upserts with zero reindex downtime.
success.quality: Reproducible nDCG@10 lift over BM25+dense RRF baseline on attribute-heavy slices of BEIR subsets and Amazon ESCI; losses published alongside wins.
success.adoption: GitHub star and PyPI download growth post-launch; >=3 external contributors; median issue first-response < 72h sustained solo.

personas.name: App developer
personas.role: Builds retrieval for attribute-rich domains (e-commerce, docs, finance)
personas.need: Hybrid search that beats pure vectors on graded multi-attribute queries, installable in one command on CPU

personas.name: Sceptical evaluator
personas.need: Every published number reproducible with one command on documented CPU hardware

personas.name: Platform integrator
personas.role: Wires KSE into an existing stack (LangChain, agent platforms, graph DBs)
personas.need: Stable interfaces, tiered backend conformance, connector points for Rainbird/Alphient-class platforms

personas.name: Solo maintainer
personas.need: Automation-heavy ops, scoped support policy, sustainable triage

inputs.docs_data: Product catalogues, document corpora, arbitrary text records via adapters (Shopify, WooCommerce, generic)
inputs.structured: User-defined dimension schema (YAML/JSON: named dimensions + descriptions + anchor examples); KG triples; backend config
inputs.events: Item add/update/delete (incremental upsert); search queries via Python API, CLI, LangChain/LlamaIndex retriever

outputs.answer_action: Fused ranked result list with per-channel provenance (embedding, conceptual, graph ranks + scores)
outputs.format: Typed Python objects; CLI quickstart; drop-in retriever interfaces; 3D conceptual-space explorer
outputs.explainability: Per-channel contribution breakdown + per-dimension scores on every result — explanation by decomposition

edge_cases.text: Score-scale mismatch across channels — must never distort fused ranking (mitigated by RRF)
Missing channel: no graph configured or no dimension schema — degrade to 2-channel/1-channel mode with explanation flag
Cold start: items queried before dimension scoring completes — serve available channels, flag partial coverage
Conflicting channel rankings — surface disagreement in per-channel breakdown rather than hiding it
Non-English corpora — embedding model default is English-biased; document limitation, allow model swap
Corpus exceeds in-memory backends — document SQLite/hnswlib limits and Tier 1/2 upgrade path

s4_system_of_record.canonical_store: User's own source systems (database, Shopify store, file corpus via adapters). SDK is projection-first: never canonical, never mutates source. (⚡ recommended — confirm)
s4_system_of_record.raw_artifacts: Optional local snapshot of ingested records with stable IDs + SHA-256 content hashes for deterministic replay and dedupe. (⚡ recommended)
s4_system_of_record.principle: Truth = user's source store. Projections = everything KSE derives (embeddings, dimension scores, graph edges, caches) — all rebuildable from source + versioned schema + pinned model IDs.
s4_system_of_record.llm_service: None by default. Optional dimension scoring: current OpenAI client API or local scorer (sentence-transformers cross-encoder) — no API key required for default path. (⚡ recommended)
s4_system_of_record.auth_service: None — in-process library; inherits host application identity/access model. Backend credentials via config, never stored.

s5_projections.training_data: Gold relevance judgements from pinned public datasets (BEIR SciFact/NFCorpus/FiQA + Amazon ESCI attribute slice) under benchmarks/; optional user click feedback for learned fusion.
s5_projections.update_cadence: Real-time incremental upserts; batch rebuild on schema/model semver bump.
s5_projections.embedding_models: Default all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (ONNX, int8); quality bge-small-en-v1.5; scale model2vec potion-base-8M (>1M items); ANN hnswlib/usearch.
s5_projections.graph_backend_tiers: T1 CI-covered: NetworkX (default), Neo4j. T2 community: ArangoDB, TypeDB. T3 connectors: Rainbird (reasoning channel), Alphient Prime (platform connector); Barnacle Alexandria adjacent/interop.

pattern: Hybrid retrieval substrate (dense + conceptual + graph, RRF-fused)

flow_steps.text: Ingest: adapter pulls item → normalise to universal record; SHA-256 content hash for dedupe/replay
Project: embed text (ONNX MiniLM default) · score dimensions vs user schema (LLM or local scorer) · upsert graph edges — all incremental
Query parse: embed query; map to dimension targets via embedding similarity against each dimension's anchor descriptions
Retrieve concurrently: vector top-k · conceptual top-k over feature store · graph traversal top-k
Fuse: RRF default (rank-based, scale-free); optional min-max normalised weighted fusion; learned fusion later opt-in
Explain: attach per-channel ranks, scores and per-dimension breakdown to every result
Fallback: failed/empty channels degrade gracefully; below-threshold fused confidence → dense-only + explicit flag

guardrails.text: Default path makes zero network calls; quickstart requires no API key (verifiable: network-mocked CI test asserts no socket use)
Simulation code isolated under simulations/ with warning headers; import from benchmarks/ is a CI failure
README performance claims must reference a benchmark artefact regenerable by make bench (CI link-check)
No CUDA/GPU package in the default dependency tree (CI asserts pip install on CPU-only image succeeds with no NVIDIA deps)
Public API fully typed; mypy clean on kse_memory public surface

s6_runtime_flow.fallbacks: Channel-level graceful degradation (EC-02); local scorer when no API key; dense-only + flag below confidence threshold (FR-07).

offline_evals.gold_set: Pinned BEIR subsets (SciFact ~5k, NFCorpus ~3.6k, FiQA sample) + Amazon ESCI attribute-heavy slice; CPU-only on GitHub-hosted runners
metrics: vs BM25 / dense-only / BM25+dense RRF baselines

online_metrics.user_feedback: GitHub issues/discussions; star and download growth around launch moments
online_metrics.incident_rate: Median issue first-response < 72h (solo-sustainable); external contributor count >= 3 in 90 days

observability.p95_latency: Latency regression test on 100k-item local corpus per release
observability.errors: CI green on every release (benchmark + integration suites)
observability.drift: Benchmark score drift vs pinned baseline flagged per release
observability.cost_per_task: Cost per 1k items on optional LLM-scoring path, tracked in bench output

s7_evals_ops.replay: Deterministic: content hash + schema version + model IDs reproduce any projection; fusion seedable; any ranked result reconstructable from source + pins.

user_stories.title: Credibility reset
user_stories.narrative: As the maintainer, I remove all unvalidated claims so the repo can be scrutinised safely.
acceptance: Given the current repo, when README v3 lands, then no unvalidated numeric claim remains, the placeholder arXiv badge is removed, status markdowns are consolidated into docs/, and simulation code lives under simulations/ with explicit labelling.

user_stories.title: Zero-dependency CPU quickstart
user_stories.narrative: As a new developer on CPU-only hardware, I get hybrid results with nothing but pip.
acceptance: Given a fresh venv on CPU-only hardware, when I run pip install kse-memory-sdk && kse quickstart, then hybrid results return in <60s with no external service, no API key, no network call, and no CUDA dependency installed.

user_stories.title: RRF fusion
user_stories.narrative: As a developer, I get scale-free fusion by default.
acceptance: Given results from >=2 channels with incompatible score scales, when fused, then RRF is applied by default and every result retains per-channel rank/score provenance.

user_stories.title: Custom dimension schema
user_stories.narrative: As a developer in any domain, I define my own conceptual dimensions.
acceptance: Given a YAML schema of named dimensions with anchors, when items are ingested, then dimensions are scored and queryable, and no hardcoded fashion vocabulary remains in the default path.

user_stories.title: Real benchmarks
user_stories.narrative: As a sceptical evaluator, I reproduce every published number.
acceptance: Given pinned BEIR/ESCI datasets, when I run make bench, then the full results table including losses regenerates in one command on documented CPU hardware.

user_stories.title: Domain packs
user_stories.narrative: As a developer, I start from worked examples, not blank schemas.
acceptance: Given the examples directory, when I open the retail, finance, or documents pack, then each ships a dimension schema plus a runnable notebook demonstrating a query pure vector search handles worse.

user_stories.title: Local scorer parity
user_stories.narrative: As an offline user, I score dimensions without an API key.
acceptance: Given no API key, when dimension scoring runs, then the local scorer produces schema-conformant scores and quickstart parity is maintained.

user_stories.title: Real domain mapping
user_stories.narrative: As a multi-domain user, cross-domain dimension mapping actually transforms values.
acceptance: Given source and target domain profiles, when map_dimensions runs, then values are transformed per the mapping definition (replacing the identity stub), with tests proving non-identity behaviour.

user_stories.title: Graph backend choice
user_stories.narrative: As a user with an existing graph DB, I plug in my preferred store without forking.
acceptance: Given the tiered backend policy, when I configure Neo4j (T1) or ArangoDB/TypeDB (T2), then the same GraphStoreInterface contract passes the shared conformance suite.
Given a Rainbird connector (T3), when enabled, then it contributes a reasoning channel to fusion without acting as the graph store of record.

user_stories.title: Learned fusion
user_stories.narrative: As an advanced user, I train fusion weights on my own relevance data.
acceptance: Given labelled query-result pairs, when learned fusion is enabled, then a logistic model over channel features is trained, evaluated against RRF, and only recommended where it wins.

user_stories.title: Launch kit
user_stories.narrative: As the maintainer, I launch deliberately once the substance is real.
acceptance: Given Phases 0-2 complete, when v3.0 ships, then Show HN post, technical blog, awesome-list PRs, and the arXiv preprint (real numbers only) are published in sequence.
